info.title: Cairnflow ingress API
info.description: Machine-readable contract of the ingress and introspection response bodies. Prose for humans: docs/admin-api.md. Every schema is JSON Schema 2020-12. Evolution rule: only **optional** fields are added; clients must ignore unknown fields (schemas leave additionalProperties open). The TS e2e suite checks every response of the paths below in strict mode (an undeclared field is an error), so the server cannot add a field without changing this file. Fields marked x-cairn-reserved are reserved for features behind a gate: today's runtime NEVER returns them. Ingress clients must be generated from this file or validated against it.

x-cairn-untimed.description: With a time filter: the number of rows excluded for lacking timestamps (summed over every range)

x-cairn-partial.description: true when a range hit the scan limit (10 000 rows or 2 s per range) — matching rows remain unscanned — or a range did not answer within 4 s (its engine is busy; that range is absent from the listing). Every listing is a bounded scan: the tenant filter reads entry 0 of every row

get.summary: The state of one invocation

x-cairn-read.description: leader = the engine holding the lease; follower = a reader, durable but possibly older than an earlier leader read

get.summary: Read one of the invocation's streams over SSE — leader only
get.description: text/event-stream. Events: record {offset, durable, step, attempt, k, data} (id: = offset), gap {offset, dropped}, superseded {offset, step, attempt}, end {next} (the stream is sealed and fully read; the server closes), moved {leader} (the leader term ended), reset {} (after moved, temporary streams only). A record's durable belongs to the record (AP-12), temporary streams are always false. Resume with ?from=<offset> or Last-Event-ID. A node not leading the range answers 503 with leader and opens no follower reader (AP-13). Permissions: user stream names need an invoke key; $log/$trace need the read capability (view or admin key). Another tenant: 404. A stream that no longer exists (a temporary stream 60 s after sealing): 410 stream_expired. Over the node's SSE connection limit: 429 sse_limit + Retry-After. :keepalive every 15 s; each connection lives at most 10 minutes.

get.summary: The invocation's log ($log) — follow=1: SSE, like /streams/$log; without follow: a JSON page {records, next} (read capability: view or admin key; leader only)
get.description: With follow=1 the body is text/event-stream, the same events as /invocations/{id}/streams/{name}. Without follow: application/json {records: [{offset, durable, step, attempt, k, ...log record}], next} — not declared as a schema here yet (the console only uses follow=1). A node not leading the range answers 503 with leader; the header x-cairn-forward: leader ⇒ runs at the leader.

200.description: SSE lines (follow=1) or a JSON page

get.description: The list of artifacts PUT with ctx.artifact.put. Readable by the tenant's invoke key. A node not leading the range answers 503 with leader; a purged invocation ⇒ 404.

get.description: content-type as given to ctx.artifact.put, cache-control immutable (content-addressed by sha). No artifact row ⇒ 404: orphaned objects or ones from a purged earlier life of the same id cannot be read through here.

key.name: key
key.description: Object key (virtual object) or workflow key (handler run)

idempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency (protocol-v1.md §8.6): the same key (within tenant, scope, service, handler, object key) ⇒ the same invocation. UTF-8, otherwise 400. A workflow run is already once per key.

limitKeyHeader.name: x-cairn-limit-key
limitKeyHeader.description: The concurrency limit's limit key. Only on the /scope/{scope}/… path; the unscoped path ⇒ 400.

limitKeyQuery.name: limit-key
limitKeyQuery.description: Like the header x-cairn-limit-key (the query wins if both are present).

logLevel.name: cairnflow-log-level
logLevel.description: The minimum ctx.log level for this invocation (goes into entry 0, overrides HandlerOptions.logLevel). Any other value ⇒ 400 before anything is created.

objectKey.name: key
objectKey.description: The object key or workflow key holding the promise

waitMs.name: wait_ms
waitMs.description: Long-poll up to min(wait_ms, --attach-max-wait-ms) (default 60 000) waiting for the invocation to stop for good; absent ⇒ --invoke-wait-ms. Client default 25 000 — under the 30 s limit of the GCP LB. Not a number ⇒ 400

scheduleName.name: name
scheduleName.description: Schedule name: 1–128 characters [A-Za-z0-9._-], unique within (tenant, scope)

tag.name: cairnflow-tag
tag.description: One user tag k=v; repeat the header for several tags. Immutable after creation; malformed ⇒ 400

x-cairn-invocation-id.description: The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach

Waiting.description: Not stopped for good yet (waiting on a timer, on a VO lock, or /send). Ask /invocations/{id} again

x-cairn-invocation-id.description: The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach

Invoke409.description: paused, already_invoked (a workflow's second run), or an error (wrong_range, …)

x-cairn-invocation-id.description: The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach

Invoke429.description: throttled (durable, with an id, Retry-After) or range_overloaded (nothing created, no id)

x-cairn-invocation-id.description: The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach

Invoke500.description: failed (the invocation's outcome, with a code) or a lower-layer error (ErrorBody, may have an id)

x-cairn-invocation-id.description: The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach
The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach

Workflow500.description: The run failed — HTTP code 500, not 200

x-cairn-invocation-id.description: The answer's invocation id — present on /invoke, /send and attach

InvocationId.description: 48 hex characters — an opaque string. Do not derive the partition from the id.

Output.description: The handler's result bytes, decoded as UTF-8 (invalid bytes replaced by U+FFFD). The TS SDK writes JSON, so this is a **string containing JSON** — the client does JSON.parse once more.

InvocationState.description: The durable state of an invocation. `waiting` is NOT part of this set: it only exists in the answers of the /invoke, /send and /workflow doors.

FailureCode.description: The code of failed/paused: the handler's HTTP-like code (TerminalError), or the runtime's 57x band — 570 journal mismatch, 571 protocol violation, 572 cancelled, 573 workflow already invoked, 574 no object key, 575 maxAttempts exhausted, 576 quarantine, 577 INFRA_STUCK, 578 journal_too_long, 579 a tenant resource limit exceeded (the message starts with timers_limit, state_keys_limit, artifacts_limit or value_bytes_limit), 580 journal_bytes_limit (paused: raise maxJournalBytes, then resume), 413 payload_too_large

InvokeThrottled.description: The permit wait limit or the rate tokens ran out: the invocation is durable and scheduled to run again

InvokeAlreadyInvoked.description: The workflow key already has a run; id is the run holding the key. Continue with /workflow/{service}/{key}/attach

InvocationStatus.description: GET /invocations/{id}. output only when completed; code + message when failed/paused.

lastFailure.description: The error of the most recent failed attempt (a handler reporting a retryable error, or an infrastructure error of the turn — code 500) — present when status is running, suspended or paused (e.g. paused 575: why the attempts ran out), and only when read from the leader (x-cairn-read: leader). Absent = no failed attempt recorded yet. message is cut at 1 KiB.

streams.description: RESERVED for streams (a feature behind a gate): every stream of the invocation. Today's runtime never returns it.

createdAt.description: When the admission committed (create_ts of entry 0). Unchanged for the invocation's whole life — through suspension, pause, migrate, split, merge; restart gets a new id and new timestamps.

modifiedAt.description: The most recent state change (create_ts of the state row)

endedAt.description: When it ended: equal to modifiedAt, only when completed/failed

attempt.description: ctx.attempt of the failed attempt (0 = the first)

atMs.description: Wall-clock time (epoch ms) when that attempt ended

nextAttemptAtMs.description: Wall-clock time (epoch ms) when the next attempt is due — only while the invocation is backing off (running, with a scheduled retry). Absent when nothing is scheduled: an attempt is running, the invocation is suspended or paused.

durableOffset.description: The last durable offset (the number of durable elements)

sealed.description: The stream is sealed (the invocation ended, paused or restart)

partition.description: The id of the range holding the invocation

service.description: Absent while entry 0 could not be read

deployment.description: The deployment the invocation is pinned to

attempt.description: Consecutive failed attempts of the pending retry appointment; 0 = none

node.description: The node that returned the row — only with ?scope=cluster

createdAt.description: When the admission committed (create_ts of entry 0). Unchanged for the invocation's whole life — through suspension, pause, migrate, split, merge; restart gets a new id and new timestamps.

modifiedAt.description: The most recent state change (create_ts of the state row)

endedAt.description: When it ended: equal to modifiedAt, only when completed/failed

partial.description: true when a node did not answer, a range is covered by nobody, or a range hit the scan limit

limit.description: the limit actually applied per range — ?limit= is clamped to 1000

untimed.description: With a time filter: the number of rows excluded for lacking timestamps, summed over every node

ErrorCode.description: A machine-readable error code. range_overloaded: 429, nothing created, resend after Retry-After. wrong_range: 409, with table. stream_expired: 410 when reading a stream whose retention expired (temporary streams: sealed + 60 s). sse_limit: 429, the node already has enough SSE connections — reconnect after Retry-After. too_many_open_streams: 429, the tenant already has --max-open-streams-per-tenant long-lived connections (stream SSE, pending attach) open on this node — reconnect after Retry-After. schedules_disabled: 409 at PUT /schedules while the schedules/table gate is not enabled (cairn-ctl cluster enable-schedules). egress_denied: 400 when the node's egress policy (--egress-*) refuses the deployment's endpoint (POST /deployments, replay check) — the message says why, without the address a name resolved to or the blocked range, and does not echo content from the destination side. payload_too_large: 413 when the body of /invoke, /send (and scoped, workflow) exceeds the tenant's max-payload=. deploy_rate_limited: 429 at POST /deployments when the tenant exceeds deploy-rate= — resend after Retry-After. key_rate_limited: 429 at every route needing a key when one API key (or SSO user) exceeds the node's --key-rate (SaaS profile 1000/1) — resend after Retry-After. identity_required: 400 at POST /deployments when the node requires request-identity verification (--deploy-require-identity, SaaS profile) but the SDK does not declare requestIdentity: v1 — enable identityKeys in serve() and register again. compression_required: 400 at POST /deployments when the node requires REQUEST_RESPONSE body compression (--deploy-require-compression, SaaS profile) but the SDK does not declare requestCompression: gzip — enable compression (the TypeScript SDK's default) and register again. key_roles_disabled: 409 at POST /admin/keys when creating a key with role view or provision while the auth/keys-v2 gate is not enabled (cairn-ctl cluster enable-key-roles). tenant_limited: 429 at every door creating new work (/invoke, /send, workflow, restart, manual schedule fire) while the tenant is in state limited — nothing created, no id. tenant_suspended: 403 at the same doors (and POST /deployments) while the tenant is suspended. tenant_state_disabled: 409 at PUT /admin/tenants/{tenant}/state while the tenants/state gate is not enabled (cairn-ctl cluster enable-tenant-state). live_invocations_limit: 429 at every door creating new work when the tenant already has maxLive live invocations (a soft limit) — nothing created, no id. deployments_limit: 409 at POST /deployments when the tenant already has maxDeployments deployments — remove old ones. schedules_limit: 409 when PUTting a new schedule while the tenant already has maxSchedules schedules. tenant_deleting: 403 for every request by key, cookie or SSO session of a deleting/purged tenant; 409 at POST /admin/keys for that tenant. tenant_purge_disabled: 409 at PUT /admin/tenants/{tenant}/state {state: deleting} while the tenants/purge gate is not enabled (cairn-ctl cluster enable-tenant-purge). tenant_purging: 409 when reverting a tenant that is past its purgingMs timestamp. tenant_purged: 409 for every PUT …/state and POST /admin/keys of a purged tenant. store_unavailable: 503 when the cell's store has a transient error on the request's read/write path — for a write it is not certain what was done, resend (with the same idempotency key) after a tick; the body carries no store details. keys_busy: 503 at POST /admin/keys and DELETE /admin/keys/{id} when the key registry keeps changing underfoot (concurrent create/revoke commands) — nothing written yet, resend after Retry-After. Not in the enum because it is not sent in the code field: POST /query reports read limits with an error starting with query_budget: (422 a query over its limit, 429 the tenant ran out of read units).

ErrorBody.description: The generic error body (401/403/400/404/409/429/500/502/503). error is a sentence for humans — do not parse it. leader only on a 503 when the node knows the leader: retry exactly once there. A 503 without leader = the cluster is electing/the range is changing, back off and ask again.

table.description: The node's range table (only when code = wrong_range)

AwakeableId.description: awk_ + invocation id (48 hex) + signal index (8 hex, ≥ 17)

signal.description: A u32 number (a built-in signal) or a non-empty string (a named signal)

value.description: The JSON payload delivered with it. Absent = Void (unlike null).

RejectRequest.description: The reject body of awakeables and promises

SignalAck.description: The answer of signal and of awakeable resolve/reject: the invocation's durable state after the delivery. Delivering the same identity again is a no-op (deduplicated in the state machine).

id.description: Invocation id (signal) or awakeable id (awakeable) — exactly the string in the path

cancelled.description: Default (hard): true = this command ended the invocation (failed 572); false = it had already stopped. mode=signal: whether the invocation had really stopped when answering

PromiseAck.description: The answer of promise resolve/reject. completed: false = the promise already had a result, this time is a no-op.

woken.description: The number of waiting invocations that were given the result (0 is valid). Only when completed

PromiseView.description: GET promise: whether it has a result yet

value.description: The value's bytes decoded as UTF-8 (a string containing JSON)

TimestampMs.description: A timestamp, Unix epoch ms, the clock of the node holding the range at commit. Monotonic within one range; across nodes it differs by the nodes' clocks. Absent = unknown (a row without timestamps).

key.description: Object key (virtual object). With a key or a scope ⇒ the run is in the target's range, overlap allow only

ScheduleSpec.description: The body of PUT /schedules/{name}. Exactly one of cron / everyMs

cron.description: 5 fields minute hour day month weekday; * , - /; month/weekday names; day and weekday ORed Vixie-style; no L W # seconds

timeZone.description: IANA, default UTC. DST taken literally: a nonexistent time does not fire, a repeated time fires twice

everyMs.description: Period, anchored at the Unix epoch; ≥ --schedule-min-period-ms (default 10 000)

input.description: The JSON input of every run (≤ 64 KiB encoded). Absent = no input

overlap.description: skip (default for an unkeyed target): if the previous run has not finished, the fire time is skipped; allow: always fire (the default and the only option for a keyed target)

jitterMs.description: Shifts the fire deadline by H(id, fire time) mod jitterMs, clamped below the next fire time

status.description: The run's state when it is in the same range as the schedule (unkeyed target), read at GET

nextAt.description: The next nominal fire time (ms); null while paused

fireAt.description: The real fire deadline of nextAt (jitter added)

upcoming.description: The next 10 fire times (GET of one schedule only)

last.description: At most the 10 most recent fire times, newest last

changed.description: PUT: the definition changed (false ⇒ no-op, nextAt does not move)

truncatedRanges.description: Ranges where the listing is incomplete (partial = true): the asking tenant's schedules exceed the limit of 1 000, the limit of 8 index chunks (2 048 schedules of every tenant) was read in that range, or the tenant's read bucket ran out

delivered.description: The run is already present in its range (ingress waits at most 10 s). false: the fire is durable but the drainer has not delivered it to the target range yet — attach may get a 404 for a while

InvocationClass.description: The query class of the state

reason.description: partial: … (missing ranges) or indexing (an index being built)

InvocationPage.description: GET /invocations?cursor=. No nextCursor means the end.

params.description: Bind parameters $1…$n in order: strings, i64 integers, bools or null. Exactly n values.

read.description: Read units: index rows + point reads

IdentityKeys.description: The tenant's request-identity keys. signing=false (the node has no CAIRNFLOW_IDENTITY_MASTER) ⇒ keys empty, requests to the SDK carry no signature.

keys.description: The published generations (two between publish and retire); active = currently signing

WhoAmI.description: The identity of the calling key. Reveals no secrets.

capabilities.description: The role's capability set, in the fixed order read, invoke, operate, provision, cluster. The console only hides/disables by this set — the server still decides; do not derive capabilities from the role's name

keyId.description: null for bootstrap keys, --no-auth and SSO sessions

kind.description: Where the key lives: bootstrap — the env's cluster-admin key (CAIRNFLOW_ADMIN_KEY/_SHA256); env — another key of the env (the control plane's provision key, a metrics token); registry — a key in the auth/keys registry; null for SSO sessions and --no-auth

bootstrap.description: true only for the bootstrap cluster-admin key (kind = bootstrap); the env's provision key is false

via.description: bearer: an API key in the header; cookie: a console session logged in with a key; sso: a console session logged in with OIDC; none: --no-auth

envLabel.description: The console's environment label (--ui-env-label: 1..24 printable ASCII characters); null when not set

clusterVersion.description: null when the node could not read the cluster version

sessionExpiresAt.description: Unix ms; only when authenticated with a session cookie

user.description: The SSO session's user; null for API keys

sso.description: Whether the request's hostname has SSO login (a client in auth/oidc)

portalUrl.description: The "switch environment" link of the hostname's OIDC client (absolute http(s)); null when absent

Deployment.description: A registered deployment (immutable; registering the same endpoint again yields a new id).

currentFor.description: Services this deployment is currently the revision of

pinnedInvocations.description: Unfinished invocations still pinned to it, counted cluster-wide. Present on GET /deployments/{id} and GET /deployments?pinned=true; absent when a range has not answered

requestIdentity.description: The identity scheme the SDK declared and that was verified at /discover — absent when the SDK does not verify requests

rrCompression.description: The negotiated REQUEST_RESPONSE body compression (the SDK declares requestCompression at /discover) — absent when bodies travel uncompressed

manifest.description: The manifest captured at registration. Only on GET /deployments/{id}

Service.description: Services per the tenant's current revision.

deployment.description: The endpoint of the current revision

ty.description: The effective type; absent for unkeyed services

JournalEntry.description: One journal entry. entry/body only with ?decode=1 — the same JSON as the entry_lite/body columns of sys_journal.

name.description: The kind's name; absent for unknown codes

JournalEntryLite.description: The decoded header. completed only for commands waiting on a result (false = still waiting).

JournalBody.description: The user body: json/utf8 ⇒ text, base64 ⇒ base64. Cut at 64 KiB (truncated).

WorkflowId.description: The run id of a workflow (service, key) — only computed, reads nothing.

ResumeAck.description: POST /invocations/{id}/resume — take it out of paused and continue within the request. 409 if not paused.

PurgeAck.description: POST /invocations/{id}/purge — purge an invocation that has stopped for good. 409 if still running (paused included).

ReplayReport.description: Replay check, read-only: the existing journal runs against the given deployment.

RestartAck.description: POST /invocations/{id}/restart — restart-as-new: the id of the new invocation.

MigrateAck.description: POST /invocations/{id}/migrate — replay is the replay-check report (null when force=true).

BatchResult.description: POST /invocations/batch/{op}: the result of each id in the order sent. status is the HTTP code the single call with the same id would return; result is the single call's 2xx body, error is the error message.

result.description: The single operation's 2xx body (CancelAck, PurgeAck, ResumeAck, RestartAck)

ManifestHandler.description: A handler in the manifest: its effective type (as in GET /services) and its own contract (not yet merged with the service's). Durations in ms

ManifestService.description: A service in the manifest captured at registration, with the shared contract — a handler declaring its own overrides it

ReplayCheck.description: Replay-check a sample of the service's unfinished invocations against the deployment — the ranges this node leads, or every node with scope=cluster (sample is the limit per node)

partial.description: scope=cluster: a node did not answer

missing.description: scope=cluster: nodes that did not answer

failures.description: A mismatch report (ReplayReport) or a failed replay ({id, error, status})

ranges.description: The ranges scanned (led by this node) — send to every node to cover the whole cluster

expect.description: Move only if the pointer is currently at this id (409 otherwise) — when two people move it at once, exactly one wins

SlowRun.description: A slow run (over the tenant's slowMs threshold) still in the node's ring

node.description: The node that recorded it (only with scope=cluster)

ArchivedInvocation.description: A purged invocation, read from the archive (the same shape as /invocations/{id} + /journal). With verify=true and a corrupt record: only {id, verified: false, error}

pattern.description: comp | comp/comp | comp/comp/comp; comp is a value or *

concurrency.description: A number, or "unlimited" (an explicit no-limit — unlike "unset", which is absent)

rate.description: Rate limit in CU/s, or "unlimited"; absent = unset

burst.description: The most CU that can accumulate; absent = equal to rate

level.description: The counter level the rule applies to: 1 = scope, 2 = L1, 3 = L2

rate.description: A number, or "unlimited" (an explicit no-limit — unlike "unset", which is absent)

warning.description: Only when a pattern contains * — * gives EACH scope its own budget, not a shared pool

PutRuleRequest.description: Add/change by pattern (or the rate limit of a whole tenant). Merge: an absent field is left alone; null in concurrency/rate/burst removes that limit back to unset

tenant.description: Instead of pattern: the rate limit of the whole tenant (does not accept concurrency)

ApiKey.description: An API key. `secret` (cf_…) only appears in the response of POST /admin/keys — the bucket keeps its SHA-256

TenantSettings.description: A tenant's settings (null = unset, the node's default applies)

limits.description: Tenants with at least one limit

states.description: Tenants not in active ⇒ their state

PutTenantSettings.description: Absent fields are kept; no field at all ⇒ 400

slowMs.description: ms; 0 = back to the node's default

retentionMs.description: ms, 0 = keep forever; null = remove the limit

maxLive.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxDeployments.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxSchedules.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxTimers.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxStreams.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxStreamRam.description: bytes ≥ 1; null = remove the limit (back to the default of 1/8 of the node's stream RAM)

maxStateKeys.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxArtifactBytes.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxJournalBytes.description: a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

maxValueBytes.description: the most logical bytes of one value (state, output, a ctx.run result); a number ≥ 1; null = remove the limit

bundles.description: Invocation ids that have a bundle

ModelUsage.description: Tokens and cost of one model in one hour; "(other)" merges the models beyond the limit of 32

MeteringHour.description: The tenant's measurements for one hour, summed over every node

models.description: model ⇒ tokens/cost; only spans with a model — the totals above also include tokens with an unknown model

sdkBytesOut.description: bytes on the wire sent to the tenant's SDK endpoint (the turns' request bodies, after compression)

sdkBytesIn.description: bytes on the wire received from the tenant's SDK endpoint

units.description: payload-weighted billing units: each durable command that became durable counts max(1, ⌈payload / 64 KiB⌉), +2 per invocation, each new artifact by bytes

Pricing.description: The token price table (micro-USD per 1 000 000 tokens)

RangeView.description: One range in the range table

leader.description: The node leading the range; null when the range has no owner yet (at startup, between two terms)

address.description: The leader's ingress port; null when the range has no owner yet

term.description: The leader's term; null when the range has no owner yet

intent.description: The split/merge intent running on the range

ClusterView.description: The cluster's range table (GET /cluster; split/merge return the table after the commit)

opId.description: Only in the response of split/merge

RangeOp.description: One split/merge operation in the node's log

partial.description: scope=cluster: a node did not answer

missing.description: scope=cluster: nodes that did not answer

RangeSuggestion.description: An auto-split proposal, or a merge proposal (reason merge: range is the left range, mergeWith the right range; proposals only, never merged automatically)

ClusterVersion.description: The cluster version and migration gates

callPrefix.description: An enabled migration gate: the `calls/prefix` gate (cairn-ctl cluster enable-call-prefix) (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

callPlacement.description: An enabled migration gate: call placement (`placement: spread`), enabled by the same command as callPrefix (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

streams.description: An enabled migration gate: the `streams/table` gate (durable streams) (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

schedules.description: An enabled migration gate: the `schedules/table` gate (server-side schedules) (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

keyRoles.description: An enabled migration gate: the `auth/keys-v2` gate (roles view/provision) (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

tenantState.description: An enabled migration gate: the `tenants/state` gate (PUT /admin/tenants/{t}/state) (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

audit.description: An enabled migration gate: the `audit/table` gate (the data-plane audit) (a control plane checks GATES against the real cell)

tenantPurge.description: An enabled migration gate: the `tenants/purge` gate (`PUT /admin/tenants/{t}/state` accepts `deleting`)

values.description: An enabled migration gate: the `values/segmented` gate (segmented values)

TenantLimits.description: Per-tenant limits of the tenants registry; null = no limit

retentionMs.description: ms to keep a finished invocation; 0 = forever; overrides --retention-ms, loses to the handler's journalRetention

maxPayload.description: the most bytes of a /invoke, /send body and of every frame the SDK writes into the journal (commands, ctx.run results, the input of continueAsNew); larger values go through ctx.artifact

maxJournal.description: the most journal entries per invocation, counting Input

deployRate.description: N/S: at most N POST /deployments within S seconds

maxLive.description: the most live invocations (running, sleeping, waiting, paused) of the tenant — a soft limit, counted per tick; reached ⇒ 429 live_invocations_limit for new work

maxDeployments.description: the most deployments of the tenant; reached ⇒ 409 deployments_limit at POST /deployments

maxSchedules.description: the most schedules of the tenant; reached ⇒ 409 schedules_limit when PUTting a new schedule

maxTimers.description: the most pending timers per invocation; over it ⇒ the invocation failed 579 timers_limit

maxStreams.description: the most user streams per invocation; a new stream over the limit is dropped (like the 17th stream)

maxStreamRam.description: the most stream RAM bytes of the tenant on each node; null = the default (1/8 of the node's stream RAM, tenant default: the whole limit); over it, records are dropped and counted in cairnflow_stream_dropped_total

maxStateKeys.description: the most state keys per object; over it ⇒ the invocation failed 579 state_keys_limit

maxArtifactBytes.description: the most total artifact bytes of the tenant (counted by LIST per tick); reached ⇒ an ArtifactPut makes the invocation failed 579 artifacts_limit

maxJournalBytes.description: the most total journal bytes per invocation; the entry that pushes the total over is not written, the invocation is paused 580 journal_bytes_limit

maxValueBytes.description: the most logical bytes of one value the SDK writes into the journal; over it ⇒ the invocation failed 579 value_bytes_limit; maxPayload only applies to the inline part

usage.description: Usage counted by a background loop — only counted when the tenant has maxLive/maxArtifactBytes; up to one tick late

KeyRevocation.description: A key's revocation state. confirmed is true only when revoked, the sessions could be LISTed and no node is pending

revoked.description: The registry just re-read no longer has the id (also for an id that never existed). false ⇒ call DELETE again

confirmed.description: Every live session has surely re-read the registry after that read

listed.description: false = the sessions could not be LISTed

truncated.description: true when there are more than 1000 reports (only when cleanup failed)

OpsReportEnvelope.description: One operations report: the object's header and the JSON `cairn-ctl` wrote

OpsReport.description: The result of one `cairn-ctl … --report-to-bucket <id>` command. Carries no secrets. `result` = the JSON `--json` prints for that command (BackupReport, PruneReport, RestoreReport, the list of backups, ClusterStatus, the gate's RepairReport)

command.description: the command name, e.g. `backup prune` — not argv

exitCode.description: 0 done, 2 bad arguments, 3 refused, 4 store error

TenantState.description: The tenant's state. limited: new work is refused (429 tenant_limited), schedules do not fire; running work runs to its outcome. suspended: like limited (403 tenant_suspended) and no turn runs at all — the engine makes no calls to the tenant's endpoints; back to active, it continues. An unknown value in the registry is read as suspended. deleting: like suspended, plus every key, cookie and SSO session of the tenant is refused (403 tenant_deleting); after the keep period (7 days) the runner really deletes the tenant's rows, objects and configuration. Reverting (PUT active/limited/suspended) is possible until purgingMs is set. purged: a tombstone after the purge — cannot change any more, the id is never issued again. PUT only accepts active, limited, suspended, deleting.

AuditRecord.description: One audit record. Unknown fields pass through verbatim.

kind.description: row: an action inside a range (same commit); intent/done: an action on an object (the intent before, the outcome after); denied: permission refusals merged per minute; noop: no-op outcomes (noop, not_found) merged per minute, with count

outcome.description: ok, noop, not_found, pending, error, denied, refused, unknown (reconciled: the outcome never came)

actor.description: key: an API key (`id` = the key id, `bootstrap:<role>` for environment keys); user: the user of an SSO session (`id` = the issuer's `sub`, with `email`, `client`)

status.description: the HTTP code of `done`; null for other kinds

count.description: the number of merged attempts of `denied`; null for other kinds

truncated.description: hit the limit of 1000 objects per request — narrow the span

hostname.description: lowercase, no port; requests to this hostname belong to this client

maxRole.description: the session's highest role — a role from the cairn_role claim is capped by it

beforeMs.description: sessions with an iat before this timestamp (Unix ms) are refused

OidcConfig.description: The cell's OIDC relying-party configuration (auth/oidc + auth/revoked) — read straight from the bucket

displayName.description: the IdP's name on the login button; null ⇒ "SSO"

issuer.description: an absolute http(s) URL, no query/fragment; compared verbatim with discovery and iss. Must pass the node's egress policy (--egress-require-https)

beforeMs.description: a timestamp computed by the caller; the cell stores max(beforeMs, cell time + 60 s) unless the row already has a timestamp ≥ beforeMs (resending does not drift). > cell time + 24 h ⇒ 400

DeploymentTransport.description: How the transport mode was chosen at registration; absent for deployments registered before this field existed

policy.description: declared: the mode the SDK declares (except the https:// rule of --deploy-https-request-response, see bidiProbe); auto: probe /discover over h2 when the SDK declares BIDI_STREAM

declared.description: the mode the SDK declares in the manifest

discoveredHttp.description: the HTTP version of the /discover call (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2)

bidiProbe.description: auto + BIDI declared: ok, or failed: <reason>; an https:// endpoint declaring BIDI on a node with --deploy-https-request-response (the saas profile) whose request does not state a transport: skipped: <reason>. failed/skipped ⇒ protocolMode is REQUEST_RESPONSE

TenantPurge.description: A tenant's purge progress, read fresh from the bucket. No run data.

state.description: The verbatim value of state= in the registry (absent = active)

deletingMs.description: When it entered deleting (ms); a string = a malformed timestamp, verbatim; null = absent

purgingMs.description: When phase B started — from here on it cannot be reverted

purgedMs.description: When the purged tombstone was written

keepMs.description: The revertible keep period of phase A on the answering node

held.description: Prefixes held in place in the trash (entries rechecked or just read during this visit)

heldComplete.description: true = held is complete; false = this visit ran out of its trash classification budget (5 s), heldUnchecked entries not yet classified may be held entries — visit again, progress is remembered

heldUnchecked.description: The number of trash entries not classified or not rechecked when the budget ran out; 0 when heldComplete

objects.description: The number of objects remaining under each prefix (limit 1000); empty prefixes are absent

lastRound.description: The runner's most recent round, if the answering node is the runner; null otherwise
